<H2> A passion project for builders <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> I have always wanted Project Zomboid to offer a building experience where a large collection stays organized, choices are easy to understand, and an entire base can be planned before spending the first plank. That idea began with my Building Menu for Build 41. <LINE> <LINE> Build 42 changed construction and introduced a new vanilla Building Menu, but the planning tools, grouped choices, detailed recipe information, flexible presentation, and multiplayer controls I wanted were still outside what the vanilla menu offered. Rather than leave those ideas behind, I started again and built Knox Buildworks around them. <LINE> <LINE> This mod is my attempt to make building feel like a complete part of the game: browse naturally, understand what a recipe will do, design large projects, share them with friends, and give server communities meaningful control without losing the fun of construction. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> <SPACE> Knox Buildworks is made for the community and continues to grow through player feedback. <POPRGB> <SPACE> If you enjoy the mod and would like to support the time that goes into it, the button below opens my Ko-fi page. Support is always optional, and playing, reporting problems, and sharing the mod are appreciated too.

<H2> Core and Vanilla Expanded <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Knox Buildworks provides the system and its converted core construction. The included Vanilla Expanded add-on is optional and adds a much larger organized collection of walls, roofs, doors, windows, floors, fences, containers, furniture, decorations, vegetation, road pieces, and survival structures. <LINE> <LINE> Other compatible add-ons can place their buildables into the same catalog and reuse its categories. Enable only the collections wanted by the server, but remember that removing one also removes its recipes from searches, plans, and rule choices. <LINE> <LINE> For multiplayer, add each chosen construction add-on to both the server mod list and Workshop list, then ensure every player downloads the same version.

<H2> Rules are shared by the server <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> When an administrator saves a valid ruleset, connected players receive the new revision. The server then checks availability, requirements, placement, blueprint access, item use, XP, and the finished construction whenever somebody builds. A client preference cannot bypass those checks. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Keep the mod list consistent <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Enable the same Knox Buildworks version and construction add-ons for the server and every player. If an add-on is removed, review rules and presets that used its categories or buildables. Ask players to reconnect after changing the server mod list or applying a major update. <LINE> <LINE> Keep exported presets as backups before a large rules change, and test with a normal player rather than only an administrator account.

<H2> Starting points <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Current Server Rules reloads the rules players are using now. Definition Defaults returns the draft to the normal Knox recipes. Disable All is useful when you want to begin with a tightly restricted server and enable only selected groups. Loading any source changes only your draft. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Share and reuse a ruleset <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Give the preset a clear name and export it to your client. Another administrator can copy that preset into their own preset folder, select Import to refresh the list, and load it as a draft on another server. <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> Loading is not the same as applying. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> Review the effective rules, select Validate and Save, and wait for the new server revision. Warnings usually mean that the preset expects buildables or add-ons that are not enabled here.

<H2> Change only what your server needs <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Each build stage can have its own material and tool requirements, minimum skills, XP rewards, required learned recipes, and construction time. Turn on an override only for the part you want to replace; everything else continues to use the normal buildable recipe. <LINE> <LINE> Requirement rows let you choose valid items or tags, how many are needed, and whether they are consumed, kept, drained by uses, or destroyed. Use alternatives when several items should satisfy the same requirement. <LINE> <LINE> Select Validate and Save when finished. The editor will point out unknown items, recipes, skills, duplicates, and invalid values before anything is applied to players. Some special Build 42 objects keep protected native requirements, but their availability, XP, and build time can still be adjusted.

<H2> Safe draft workflow <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Authorized administrators open Build Rules from the ElyonLib dock. The editor copies the synchronized server document into a private draft; browsing, loading a preset, and changing controls do not affect players. Validate and Save must succeed before the server publishes a new revision. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Editor layout <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select a category, subcategory, or buildable on the left, then select a stage and tab on the right. Availability, inputs, finishes, skills and XP, recipe knowledge, and time are separate controls. The Finishes tab can waive plaster, paint, or wallpaper materials for every wall, while selected walls can explicitly inherit, require, or waive each cost. Non-wall paintable objects keep their normal requirements. Reload discards the draft and requests current server data. Reset Selected removes that buildable's overrides. <LINE> <LINE> Concurrent saves use revision checks. If another admin saves first, reload the newer revision before applying your changes.

<H2> Menu and planning <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Replace vanilla Build Menu decides whether the sidebar Build button opens Knox Buildworks directly. Enable Planning Mode controls blueprint UI availability. Max planned buildables limits ghosts per blueprint, while Blueprint radius limits the square area around its first anchor. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Construction and water <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Build XP multiplier scales Knox construction awards. Water well supply selects infinite or limited-and-refilling behavior; limited mode also uses capacity, initial fill, groundwater-per-hour, and rain-refill settings. <LINE> <LINE> Sandbox options are separate from Build Rules. Use sandbox controls for global systems and limits; use Build Rules for category, subcategory, buildable, and stage policy.

<H2> Category to buildable <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Availability is checked from category, to subcategory, to individual buildable. Inherit means that level follows the broader setting. A more specific choice can create an exception. <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Disable a whole category when it does not fit the server. <LINE> Re-enable one useful subcategory inside it. <LINE> Disable or re-enable a single buildable for a final exception. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> The Effective Status line shows what players will actually receive. Use the broadest sensible rule first, then add only the exceptions you need.

<H2> Test Runner <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Use the Test Runner when an add-on or update introduces many buildables and you want a quick health check. Its filters help you find entries with missing sprites, incomplete stages, bad requirements, or unsupported special objects. Select a result to focus on the affected buildable. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Tile Browser <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The Tile Browser lets you search the loaded tile library and inspect a sprite's visible properties. It is useful when a placed object behaves differently from its preview, when checking storage capacity, or when identifying the correct face of a multi-direction object. <LINE> <LINE> These tools help locate problems; always finish by placing and using the object in the actual world.

<H2> A safe way to change server rules <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> 1. Reload Current Server Rules before editing. <LINE> 2. Export a named preset so you can return to the current setup. <LINE> 3. Prefer a category or subcategory rule when many related pieces need the same treatment. <LINE> 4. Use individual buildable and stage overrides only for exceptions. <LINE> 5. Review Effective Status and validate every edited section. <LINE> 6. Save and wait for the confirmation that a new revision was synchronized. <LINE> 7. Join as a normal player and try the affected recipes, plans, and permissions. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> If the result is not what you intended, reload the saved backup preset, review it, and apply it through Validate and Save.

<IMAGECENTRE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/Button_Gear.png,28,28> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Knox UI Appearance <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Choose a theme, high contrast, panel opacity, and checkerboard, light, dark, or custom object-preview backgrounds. A checkerboard makes both very dark and very light objects easier to distinguish. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Readability controls <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Fade unavailable buildable icons is an on/off toggle. Disable it when dimmed objects are hard to recognize; readiness borders and building restrictions remain active. Grid, detailed list, and compact views let you choose between more information and less screen coverage. <LINE> <LINE> If you use a larger game font, widen or raise the panel when you want more details, or use compact mode for a smaller footprint. Drag the resize corner after changing modes. Appearance choices are personal and do not affect other players.

<H2> Using the construction cursor <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select Build, move the preview to the desired square, rotate or change its face when available, and confirm on a valid location. Many compatible buildables stay on the cursor so you can place several in a row while you still have the required materials. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> If the preview is invalid <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Look for occupied tiles, missing support, the wrong side of a wall, a required floor or frame, poor light, distance, or something blocking part of a multi-tile footprint. Stairs, gates, large furniture, and irregular objects need every tile in their footprint to be valid. <LINE> <LINE> When the timed action finishes, the recipe uses its materials, keeps or wears its tools as described, awards its XP, and creates the finished object.

<H2> Search and filters <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Search can look through buildable names, requirements, or everything at once. Combine it with category pages and the type, material, and skill filters to narrow a very large collection. Clear a filter or return to All when something expected is not visible. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Fast navigation <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Favorites keeps hand-picked recipes together. <LINE> Recent returns to recipes used lately. <LINE> Sorting changes the order without changing availability. <LINE> Category arrows reveal additional category pages. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <IMAGE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/FavouriteYes.png,20,20> The star changes only your personal favorite list. A server-disabled buildable remains unavailable even when it is a favorite.

<H2> Families instead of duplicate recipes <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Related pieces are often gathered into one buildable family. Use the arrows to move between roof shapes, wall pieces, furniture models, directions, or construction qualities instead of searching for a separate entry for every sprite. <LINE> <LINE> Material, colour, model, and finish selectors appear when that family supports them. The preview and requirements follow your selection, and the same choice is remembered when you place a plan. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Check the preview before placing. <POPRGB> <SPACE> Members of one family may have different dimensions or may need a wall, floor, frame, or open space.

<H2> Reading the inspector <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> The right-hand inspector shows the selected name, description, preview, useful properties, dimensions, readiness, skills, and materials. Dimensions appear as width x depth x height beneath the preview, so you can judge the space needed before starting placement. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Storage capacity <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Storage is shown for one usable face instead of repeating the same information for every rotation. <INDENT:18> <LINE> Multi-tile objects list every tile that provides storage on that face. <LINE> A two-tile dumpster can therefore show two separate capacities. <LINE> Multiple compartments on one tile, such as Fridge and Freezer, are listed separately. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Important: <POPRGB> <SPACE> previewed capacity describes the finished object. A blueprint ghost cannot hold items.

<H2> Before and after construction <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A material or finish selector changes the planned construction variant. Supported world actions can later apply plaster, paint, signs, or other finishes to a finished target. Each action still checks its normal tools, resources, skills, and target type. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Paintable objects <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Paintable furniture uses the object's custom color, matching the vanilla painting approach. White military crates are the neutral color base; green and gray military crates are also recognized by the Knox painting system. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Painting changes appearance only. <POPRGB> <SPACE> It does not alter container capacity, construction XP, recipe requirements, collision, or ownership.

<H2> More than decoration <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Storage furniture, fridges and freezers, doors, windows, lights, work surfaces, appliances, wells, and other supported objects keep the gameplay functions appropriate to them after construction. Multi-tile storage can provide a container on more than one tile, while one appliance tile can have separate compartments such as Fridge and Freezer. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Water wells <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Depending on the server settings, built wells either provide an unlimited source of clean water or hold a limited supply that slowly returns through groundwater and rain. If a limited well is empty, give it time or wait for rainfall. <LINE> <LINE> Read the inspector before building to see dimensions, storage capacity, and other useful properties of the selected object.

<H2> When one player cannot build <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Check that character's materials, tools, skills, learned recipes, light, distance, and blueprint access. Select the buildable again to read the missing requirement, then try the placement cursor on a suitable square. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> When everyone has the same problem <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Ask an administrator whether the buildable or its category was disabled and whether Planning Mode is allowed. Everyone should use the same versions of Knox Buildworks and its enabled add-ons. After a server or mod update, reconnect before testing again. <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> The server makes the final decision. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> It checks the recipe, position, permissions, item use, XP, and finished object so every player sees the same result.

<IMAGECENTRE:media/ui/inventoryPanes/Button_Pin.png,28,28> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Keep requirements visible <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Select the pin on a buildable to keep its recipe visible after the catalog closes. The pinned panel updates readiness, materials, tools, skills, and learned-recipe knowledge as the character and inventory change. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Pinned panel options <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Collapse individual recipes, move the panel when manual positioning is selected, and use its gear menu for alignment, position mode, opacity, accent bar, and icon or text presentation. <LINE> <LINE> Pinned recipes are a client convenience. They do not reserve items, start a queue, or change the server recipe.

<H2> Plans are editable ghosts <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Place Plan adds a ghost to the active blueprint instead of building immediately. Planning Mode can create, duplicate, rename, delete, activate, and move blueprints, subject to access rights and server limits. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Layout tools <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Place individual buildables on the chosen level. <LINE> Draw, update, and erase room layouts. <LINE> Change levels for multi-storey planning. <LINE> Move the blueprint origin or erase incorrect placements. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> Ghosts provide no collision, storage, water, light, or protection until constructed. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> The server can disable Planning Mode or limit placements and blueprint radius.

<H2> Gather area <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Contributors can mark an area used to search supported containers and vehicles for construction resources. The area belongs to the blueprint and can be moved or cleared. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Building a plan <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Build Selected targets one planned placement. Build All queues valid ghosts and works through them in order; Stop Queue cancels the remaining queue. Each construction still performs readiness, reach, placement, permission, and server validation. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> <SPACE> The queue does not create missing resources or bypass locked recipes. <POPRGB> <SPACE> If it stops, inspect the next ghost, character inventory, gather area, path, and current permissions.

<IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Book_16.png,20,20> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Light_16.png,20,20> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/BuildProperty_Clock_16.png,20,20> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> What Ready checks <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Materials, retained tools, drained uses, skills, learned recipes, light, reach, stage rules, and server availability can all affect readiness. Counts show available versus required amounts. Alternatives are grouped so any permitted item or tag can satisfy that input. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Requirement types <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> Consumed items disappear when used. <LINE> Retained tools must be present but are normally kept. <LINE> Drainable inputs remove uses rather than the entire item. <LINE> Destroyed inputs are deliberately removed by the recipe. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <BHC> Ready in the catalog is guidance, not a promise that every world square is valid. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> Placement performs the final world and server checks. Fading unavailable icons can be turned off in Knox UI Appearance without changing any rule.

<H2> Building together <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> A blueprint owner can keep a plan private or give access to everyone, a faction, or individual players. View access lets someone see the plan. Build access lets them construct its ghosts. Contribute access also lets them edit placements, rooms, and the gather area. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Taking a plan elsewhere <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> You can write a selected plan onto a supported in-game blueprint item and import a carried blueprint later. Planning Mode also provides local export and import controls for sharing a plan outside the game. An imported plan appears near the importing player so it can be moved into position. <LINE> <LINE> Access and ownership are not carried over as free permissions. The destination world or server still decides what the player may see, edit, and build.

<IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/Icon_Grid.png,24,24> <SPACE> <IMAGE:media/ui/craftingMenus/Icon_List.png,24,24> <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Choose the view that suits you <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Grid view gives each buildable a large visual card. Detailed list view shows more names, categories, and status information at once. Compact mode uses a side list of subcategories and a dense icon grid, making it useful when you want a quick overview or a smaller window. <LINE> <LINE> Selecting an icon in compact mode still gives you the available group, quality, model, material, and finish choices at the bottom. Hover over an icon to read its name and requirements. <LINE> <LINE> <PUSHRGB:0.88,0.78,0.40> Tip: <POPRGB> <SPACE> drag the bottom-right corner to find a comfortable size. The layout adapts to the current font size and available space.

<H2> Welcome to Knox Buildworks <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> Knox Buildworks gives you one organized place to discover, preview, plan, and construct buildings and objects. Open it from the building sidebar or with the configurable catalog key, which is F7 by default. It can live beside the vanilla Building Menu, or a server can make Knox the primary building action. <LINE> <LINE> <H2> Build something <TEXT> <LINE> <LINE> <INDENT:18> 1. Browse or search for what you want. <LINE> 2. Choose its quality, model, material, colour, or finish when those choices are available. <LINE> 3. Check what it needs and whether the current character is ready. <LINE> 4. Select Build to construct now, or Place Plan to leave a blueprint ghost for later. <INDENT:0> <LINE> <LINE> <GHC> Ready means your character passes the recipe checks shown in the catalog. <RGB:0.92,0.91,0.88> <SPACE> The placement cursor will then check the chosen location.
